units: <cite ref="Mishnah Berakhot 9:1">Ber. IX, 1</cite> <he>הרואֶה מקום וכ׳</he> he who sees (comes to) a place &c.
<cite ref="Berakhot 56b:9">Ib. 56ᵇ</cite> <he>הרואה נהר בחלום</he> he who sees a river in his dream.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 82a:4">B. Bath. 82ᵃ</cite> <he>כל שרואה פני חמה</he>, v. <cite ref="C00571"><he>גֶּזַע</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 56:1">Gen. R. s. 56</cite> <he>רוֹאִים אתם … רואה</he> do you see what I see? <cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 3:12">Ex. R. s. 3</cite> <he>אתה רואה ראייה אחת וכ׳</he> thou seest only one vision, but I see two; <he>אתה רואה אותן באין וכ׳</he> thou seest them come to Sinai and receive my Law, but I see &c.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 73b:8">B. Mets. 73ᵇ</cite> <he>רָאִיתָ שאינו וכ׳</he> if thou observest that he does not conduct himself properly; a. v. fr.—
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 52a:26">Snh. 52ᵃ</cite> <he>הֵנִרְאֶה מי וכ׳</he> (Ms. M. <he>הֵא נראה</he>) well, we shall see which &c., v. <cite ref="S00095"><he>קָבַר</he></cite>.

Sabb. 150ᵃ לא יאמר … הנראה שתעמור וכ׳ one must not say to one’s neighbor (on the Sabbath), well, we shall see (I am confident) that you will be with me in the evening (for business); Ab. Zar. 7ᵃ (Tosaf. = הֲנִרְאֶה בעיניך, Nif. is it pleasing to thee?); Tosef. Sabb. XVII (XVIII), 11 נראה ed. Zuck. (Var. הנ׳).
<cite ref="Sifrei Bamidbar 84:1">Sifré Num. 84</cite> <he>הנראה שתגיע עמנו וכ׳</he> be sure to arrive with (meet) us at &c.
Ib. הנ׳ שתעמידני וכ׳ be sure to wake me up, for I &c.—ר׳ דם, ר׳ קרי &c. to have an attack, be affected with.
<cite ref="Yevamot 76a:4">Yeb. 76ᵃ</cite> <he>לא ר׳ קרי מימיו</he> he never had a nightly pollution.

<cite ref="Mishnah Zavim 1:1">Zab. I, 1</cite> <he>ר׳ אחת … ובשלישי ר׳ שתים</he> (sub. <cite ref="G00263"><he>זיבה</he></cite>) if he felt one attack of gonorrhœa …, and on the third day he had two attacks.
<cite ref="Mishnah Berakhot 3:6">Ber. III, 6</cite> <he>רָאֲתָה נדה</he> (sub. <cite ref="D00867"><he>דם</he></cite>) felt menstruation.
<cite ref="Berakhot 26a">Ib. 26ᵃ</cite> <he>ר׳ זיבה</he> felt a flux; a. fr.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 83a:5">B. Bath. 83ᵃ</cite> <he>רוֹאִין … כאילו וכ׳</he> we consider the central vine-trees as if not existing.

Erub. I, 5 רואין אותה … מתכת we consider it (the cross-piece of straw or reeds) as if it were of metal; עקומה רואין וכ׳ if it is curved, we consider it as if it were straight. Gen. R. l. c. הוי רואה דמיו וכ׳ look upon the blood of this ram, as if it were the blood of &c.; a. v. fr.—מה ר׳ what did he see?, what was the reason; in gen. why? B. Bath. 123ᵃ מה ר׳ יעקב שנטל וכ׳ what reason had Jacob to take the birthright from Reuben? Pes. 53ᵇ מה רָאוּ … שמסרו וכ׳ what did Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah have in mind (how did they reason) when they were ready to give up their lives &c.? Sifré Deut. 307 מה ראו … שנשטפו וכ׳ why were the men of the flood drowned &c.?; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to see the reason of, to like, choose, prefer, approve of.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Ketubot 13:3">Keth. XIII, 3</cite>, sq. <he>רואה אני את רברי וכ׳</he> I like the opinion of Admon.
<cite ref="Ketubot 109a">Ib. 109ᵃ</cite> <he>כל מקום שאמר … רואח אני וכ׳</he> wherever R. G. said, I like &c., that opinion is the adopted rule.

Ab. II, 7 רואה אני … מדבריכם I prefer what El. … said to what you said; a. fr.—Part. pass. רָאוּי; f. רְאוּיָה; pl. רְאוּיִים, רְאוּיִין; רְאוּיוֹת chosen, selected; designated, predestined; fit, worthy, adapted (v. חֲזִי).
<cite ref="Bekhorot 59b">Bekh. 59ᵇ</cite>, a. e. <he>מנין הר׳</he>, v. <cite ref="M01786"><he>מִנְיָן</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Chullin 83b">Ḥull. 83ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>כל הר׳ לבילה</he> whatever is capable of being mixed, v. <cite ref="B00615"><he>בִּילָה</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Niddah 6:4">Nidd. VI, 4</cite> <he>כל הר׳ לדון וכ׳</he> whoever is fit (authorized) to give judgment in a criminal court, is fit &c.
<cite ref="Shabbat 89b:6">Sabb. 89ᵇ</cite> <he>ר׳ היה יעקב וכ׳</he> Jacob was destined to go down to Egypt in iron chains, but his merits were the cause (that no such force was used).
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 107a">Snh. 107ᵃ</cite> <he>ר׳ היתה וכ׳</he> Bathsheba … was predestined (as wife) for David, only he anticipated fate, v. <cite ref="Q00041"><he>פַּגָּה</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Berakhot 4a:18">Ber. 4ᵃ</cite> <he>ר׳ היו ישראל ליעשות וכ׳</he> it had been intended that a miracle be performed for the Israelites in Ezra’s days, as it has been in Joshua’s time, but sin was the cause (that it was not done).
<cite ref="Niddah 60a:21">Nidd. 60ᵃ</cite> <he>ר׳ לראות</he> fit (old enough) to have menstruation; a. v. fr.

senses.gloss: to be seen, be visible; to appear; to seem.
units: <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 48:9">Gen. R. s. 48</cite> <he>נִרְאִין כאוכלין וכ׳</he> they had the appearance of eating, one course after the other being removed.

<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 21:1">Pesik. R. s. 21</cite> <he>בפנים הרבה נ׳ להם וכ׳</he> the Lord appeared to them at Sinai with various expressions of countenance. Pesik. Vayhi, p. 5ᵃ <he>קרסי זהב נראין … הנראין וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="S02113"><he>קֶרֶס</he></cite>.

Ḥag. 2ᵃ; Snh. 4ᵇ, a. e. (ref. to יראה, Ex. XXIII, 17) יִרְאֶה יֵרָאֶה … לִרְאוֹת … לֵירָאוֹת you may read it yireh (he shall see, the Lord) or yeraëh (he shall be seen): as He comes to see, so does He come to be seen (i.e. he that is blind in one eye is exempt from visiting the Temple.
Ḥag. 5ᵇ הנראין ואינן רואין … הרואים יאינן נראין, v. קָבַל I, Hif.—
<cite ref="Pesachim 53a:8">Pes. 53ᵃ</cite> <he>שנ׳ כמקדיש וכ׳</he> it looks as if he dedicated his animal as a sacrifice, and were to eat sacred meat outside of the Temple.
<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 2:3">Ab. II, 3</cite> <he>נראין כאוהבין וכ׳</he> they appear to be friends as long as it profits them; a. v. fr.
<cite ref="Yoma 64a">Yoma 64ᵃ</cite>, v. <cite ref="D00397"><he>דָּחָה</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Sukkah 33b:7">Succ. 33ᵇ</cite> <he>נ׳ ונדחה חוזר ונ׳</he> what had been fit at one time of the Holy Day, and was discarded (on account of a temporary unfitness), may again become fit (for use on the same day); a. e.

senses.gloss: to be liked, approved of; to appear reasonable.
units: <cite ref="Chullin 108b">Ḥull. 108ᵇ</cite> <he>נ׳ דברי וכ׳</he> R. Judah’s opinion is acceptable in the event that no stirring has taken place.
<cite ref="Chullin 109a:3-7">Ib. 109ᵃ</cite> <he>נ׳ דברי ר׳ י׳ בהא</he> … <he>בהא</he> R. Judah’s opinion is acceptable in such a case, and that of the scholars in such a case.
Ber. 33ᵇ ר׳ חייא … נראין R. Ḥ. bar Abba reported Rabbi to have said nirin (it seems acceptable), contrad. to מטין a. מודים; Erub. 46ᵇ; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to cause to see; to show. Pesik. Shek., p. 19ᵃ (ref. to Ex. XXX, 13) כמין מטבע … והֶרְאֵהוּ למשה וכ׳ the Lord took a sort of a coin of fire from under his throne of glory and showed it to Moses, saying, ‘this they shall give’, like this &c.
units: <cite ref="Exodus 30:13">Ib.</cite> p. 18ᵇ <he>הקטנה ה׳ לדוד וכ׳</he> he (Joab) produced before David the smaller census, the larger he did not.

<cite ref="Kiddushin 48b">Kidd. 48ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Bava Batra 165a">B. Bath. 165ᵃ</cite>, a. e. <he>מרְאֶה מקום הוא לו</he> he merely indicated the place to him, v. <cite ref="S01732"><he>קְפֵידָא</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Berakhot 55b:3">Ber. 55ᵇ</cite> <he>מראין לו חלום טוב</he> is shown a good dream (vision).
<cite ref="Berakhot 55b:18">Ib.</cite> <he>הֶרְאוּהוּ חלומו וכ׳</he> was shown his own dream and the interpretation of his fellow prisoner’s dream.
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 5a:9">Ab. Zar. 5ᵃ</cite> <he>ה׳ לו הקב״ה לאדם דור וכ׳</he> the Lord allowed Adam to see each coming generation and its preachers &c.
<cite ref="Taanit 10b:6">Taan. 10ᵇ</cite> <he>אל תַּרְאוּ עצמכם וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="U00159"><he>שָׂבֵעַ</he> I</cite>; a. v. fr.—ה׳ פנים

senses.gloss: [to show a (friendly) face,] to visit the mourner. Y. M. Kat. III, 82ᵇ מפני … להַרְאוֹת וכ׳ why is it recommended to visit the mourner (on the Sabbath, when no other mourning ceremonies are otherwise observed)? Ib. 83ᵃ bot. אין מראין וכ׳ a mourner is not visited on New Year’s Day &c.
units: <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 100:9">Gen. R. s. 100</cite>; a. e.—
senses.label: a

units: <cite ref="Sanhedrin 93b:3">Snh. 93ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <he>איש תאר</he>, <cite ref="I Samuel 16:18">I Sam. XVI, 18</cite>) <he>שמראה פנים בהלכה</he> he makes faces shine when he argues; <cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 13:20">Num. R. s. 13</cite>; (<cite ref="Ruth Rabbah 4:3">Ruth R. to II, 1</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 125:1">Yalk. Sam. 125</cite> <he>שמאיר</he>); a. e.
senses.label: b

senses.gloss: to be shown. Y. M. Kat. III, 82ᶜ top אם הוּרְאוּ לו רוב פנים if most of the faces have been shown him, i.e. if the majority of comforters have been to see him (v. supra).

units: <cite ref="Taanit 10b:6">Taan. 10ᵇ</cite> <he>שכח … אל יִתְרָאֶה בפני הצבור</he> if he forgot and ate and drank (in a place where a fast is held), he must not show himself before the people.
